hypotheses.statement: The settlement-worker concurrency increase from 8 to 32 workers at 15:55:00Z caused database connection pool exhaustion because the pool size remained at 20, leading to pool_timeout errors affecting approximately 38% of attempts.

The feature-flag service token expiry at 15:59:00Z caused calls to flags.internal to return 401 invalid_token, leading to settlement failures affecting approximately 31% of attempts, independent of the connection pool issue.
The settlement failure ratio of 0.61 was caused by the combined effect of both the connection pool exhaustion and the feature-flag token expiry, with each contributing independently to failures.

observed_facts.statement: Configuration change at 15:55:00Z raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers, with database connection pool size left at 20.
settlement-worker database connection pool exhausted from 15:58:10Z with pool size 20, checked-out 20, queue depth rising, causing pool_timeout errors affecting approximately 0.38 of attempts.
The service token settlement-worker uses for flags.internal expired at 15:59:00Z on 2026-02-11 after being issued for 90 days on 2025-11-13, with renewal not automated.
settlement-worker calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token from 15:59:02Z, affecting approximately 0.31 of attempts, overlapping with pool_timeout failures on some attempts.
Alert settlement-failures fired at 16:00:44Z with settlement attempts failing reaching 0.61 against objective of 0.02, clearing at 18:12:30Z.
INC-2201 opened at 16:05:00Z with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing', recording no settlement value at risk.
settlement-worker connection pool raised to 64 at 17:20:15Z, pool_timeout errors stopped, and settlement failure ratio fell from 0.61 to 0.29.
Replacement token for flags.internal installed at 18:12:10Z, 401 responses stopped, and settlement failure ratio fell from 0.29 to 0.004.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or configuration management records explaining why database connection pool size is not derived from worker concurrency
open_questions.question: Why is the database connection pool size not derived from the worker concurrency?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Inventory of all service tokens with their renewal policies and automation status
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal and require auditing?

summary: Incident dual-cause-payments involved two independent faults: (1) database connection pool exhaustion due to increased worker concurrency without corresponding pool size adjustment, and (2) feature-flag service token expiry causing authentication failures. Both contributed to settlement failures peaking at 61%. Resolution required increasing connection pool size and replacing the expired token.

timeline.statement: Configuration change raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers, database connection pool size remained at 20.
Database connection pool exhausted, pool_timeout errors affecting ~38% of attempts.
Calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token, affecting ~31% of attempts.
Alert fired: settlement failure ratio reached 0.61 against objective of 0.02.
INC-2201 opened with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing'.
Connection pool raised to 64, pool_timeout errors stopped, failure ratio fell to 0.29.
Replacement token installed, 401 responses stopped, failure ratio fell to 0.004.
